**Key observations:**

1. **Affected part**: Cut stem section placed in a beaker of clear water — this is a lab/field diagnostic test.
2. **Visual feature**: Milky-white bacterial ooze is clearly streaming out of the cut stem end into the water below (visible as cloudy tendrils in the water).
3. **Stem cross-section**: Shows brown/tan vascular discoloration at the cut surface — classic internal browning of xylem vessels.

**Reasoning:**

This image shows the classic **bacterial streaming test** (also called the ooze test). A stem section is cut and suspended in water; if bacterial wilt is present, bacterial cells stream from the vascular bundles into the water as visible white streamers. This is the textbook diagnostic for **Bacterial Wilt** (*Ralstonia solanacearum*). The internal vascular browning and streaming are both pathognomonic for this disease. None of the other classes (fungal diseases, viral diseases, other bacterial diseases) produce this ooze streaming pattern.
